review_text:
Open for business in the iconic Odessa space & I felt all those feelings from eons ago.
It's a counter with cushioned seating, booths & a bar are. Pretty awesome space.
Ate:
Superiority burger
Lentils with cornbread 
Steamed veggies with tahini
Sour cherry tart with vegan chocolate gelato
Total $64 after tip
I'm not veg or vegan per de but fine more & more often vegan & veg.
There's lots of cute kitschy touches like plastic bags from spots like L&B & am Odeon sign.
The pie case is a treasure! Paper placemats with local businesses make it so fun. The cushiony counter seats or booths are the jam.
I loved my mains- especially the lentils. I didn't know the veggies were served cold but they were excellent with tahini and smack sauce(hot sauce)
The tart came with something else & I requested chocolate (vegan) gelato. That dessert was banging. Please sir I want some more.

Um, so I think I have a problem... I don't think I'll be able to stop coming to Superiority Burger for as long as I am a New Yorker so that pretty much means forever. 

I would always past the original location on my way to Confectionery and not know what was going on there. It was always busy with people standing about on the tiny block that is 9th street. 

Once again today, on my way to Confectionery I was in the neighborhood.  My phone was on its last leg and I was getting hungry so I decided to stop near somewhere local. Looking up the address, I was able to see that SB had moved but was not too far. As I approached I saw the long line and hopped on since it was nearing the opening time.

I am so happy I stopped by today which was coincidentally their opening weekend. This place is truly amazing! No matter how good the food is, if the service is not it, then the place is not a place I want to be. The team at SB was beyond hospitable despite the stress that comes with an opening weekend. The food was amazing. The Superiority Burger might be my favorite burger beating the one I had in Paris. The lentils and cornbread was delicious and comforting. I want to order it again on Monday (yes, I will be back so soon since I'm off) but I think I should try some other items. I thought I was smitten with burger but the banana bread is truly phenomenal. It is probably my favorite dessert ever and I'm not even a banana person. Every part of it was a star. The chocolate, the gelato, the, candied walnuts, and of course the banana bread itself. 
 

I wish I had asked for her name (she was the best... kind, helpful, and funny... so much so I kept ear hustling her convos with my neighboring patrons) but the server who attended to my section mentioned that they're planning to be open pretty much all day. SB has got me saying I can't wait for Monday (I'm shocked too... yeah I'm definitely not going to attempt Saturday or Sunday though lol).

We missed you, Superiority burger! I went in knowing there would be a crazy wait so we put our name down at 630 and walked around / got drinks then at 830 were seated. Everything was exactly how it used to be, same quirky funny vibes and decor, really simple tasty food, and amazing desserts, just in a much bigger space. The food and desserts were delicious. They added alcoholic drinks, but I would skip cocktails next time, as they are expensive for what they are - they have beer/wine though! but overall we loved it all.

I didn't think it was possible to improve on the original SB -- my go to for the better part of a decade(!) -- but wow, Brooks and team crushed it. It was worth the wait! The staff is lovely, the vibes are just perfect, the soundtrack remains Manhattan's finest, the seltzer really is the best, and the expanded menu hits every sort of spot. 

The collard sandwich, stuffed cabbage, and lentils were sleeper hits for us, but of course the classic megamouth and yuba sandwiches totally slayed as always. We arrived around 915p, expected a 40m wait at the bar and got to sit down in about 15m. Can't wait to become a regular.

The food is highly overrated. There is much better vegan food not only in NYC but in the East Village itself within a 0.5 radius. As a neighborhood resident; I think this is a Mecca for pretentious hipsters who actually haven't bothered to look beyond the hype of superiority and feel superior by eating overpriced mediocre vegan food. In addition, this place lacks the family vibe and neighborhood-y warm ness that is a signature of the east village. I was in the park nearby (no bathroom) and asked them if my 2.5 year old could use their bathroom to pee and they showed me the door. I wish cold mean people like that could stay away from our neighborhood!

Back and better than ever. They've really captured that energy of waiting for your food outside the old Superiority Burger, only this time inside the restaurant. It's kind of loud and buzzy and fun as hell. And still delicious -- you'll find a similar sandwich/side menu plus more desserts this time (this part of the menu deserves a thorough exploration, though the gelato and sorbet are probably still the champs). Love the bar in the back too.
Travel far to get there and was told no take out not sure if you are  doing good business been closed for a few  years almost and now open with limitations !

This place came in clutch. It was a Saturday night. My girls and I were in search of some good vegetarian food.
We head in here, and to our delight, it's vegan and vegetarian options only. They don't have many menu items. However, what we did try was good. 
I had the namesake burger, and it was just alright. Nothing really special.None of the burgers are served with fries, but it's quite filling. 
My friend had the sloppy dave  burger, which was full of seasoning it was sooo good. 
For dessert, we had the funnel cake it was a 10 out of 10 . This other desert with vegan ice cream I forget the name of right now. We also had the sweet potatoes but purple skin kind known throughout the caribbean it was a tasty fusion dish. 
Most of the staff is really friendly and attentive. 
They serve cocktails. The space is small but welcoming . I'd visit again.

The wait is long, but the one star review is not about that. It's about the food itself and the service. The portions are tiny and extremely expensive. The sweet potato is HALF of a tiny baby sweet potato that was three inches long. It was almost funny when the server put it on the table how comically small it was. The roasted beets came in a tiny cup. The burger has always been on the small side, even at the old location. And the yuba sandwich was like a kid's portion. The rhubarb pie fit in the palm of my hand, the size of an Oreo cookie. On top of the tiny overpriced portions, the wait staff is obsessed with turnover so as soon as you lift the last bite in midair, someone whisks your plate away... before you've even put your fork in your mouth. That didn't happen only once, it happened every time with every single one of our dishes. It's very uncomfortable, rude, and rushed. We spent over a hundred dollars on dinner for two plus a couple drinks (the aforementioned dishes were the only ones we ordered) and they had us out in less than an hour (after waiting 1.5 for a table). The server kept asking us if we needed anything else, bombarded our table with the check and credit card machine within one minute of finishing dessert. It was bizarre and the whole experience was awful. If you don't mind spending $150 (with tip) on a 35 minute rushed meal of meager child's portions with every busser and server snatching your plates away and pushing the check on you... then this is your place. Others, stay away.

It's a shame to see people tanking the reviews over silly stuff, because the food is outstanding. The service is typically very quick, and they've retained the vibe of the old SB except with seating and a greatly expanded menu. 

This isn't some fancy five star dining experience. You're not going to be treated like a special pretty princess. I like it that way, personally. And I'm glad to see that it's busy with a long wait - I want SB to succeed so I can keep coming here forever! You do you, SB. Just don't ever take those beets off the menu.

What was once a great fairly priced hole in the wall is now a rich person's Instagram spot.

The food is still good but portions have been traded for style and priced to accomodate the new sky rocketed rents that the rich will pay.

The worst part is the new service. We arrived at 7pm and told there wasn't an empty table until 9:45pm. As with 99% of places in the city, this reasoning is a tactic. Usually you can wait it out and people will drop their tables and bump up your reservation. Not here I guess, if you're locked in, you are a sucker. The host said we could put our name in and could sit in the back for drinks. We sat there the full 2.5 hours after group after group of walk-ins were seated before us. Okay maybe they were working a new system, fine. After 2 hours I received a text that my table was almost ready. I walked up to host and told her we were told to close out the bar tab and she would come get us. 10 minutes go by and nothing. I wait another 5 and return to the host who said they were about to seat us, and then another 15 minutes go by. I finally just stood at the front until she asked me if I'd like to make a reservation...I told her we already have a table we're waiting for. Oh suddenly one of the tables was ready.

Our food came pretty quick. 2 sandwiches, 2 sides, 1 drink and all very small portions for the wait put us over $100 not including tip. Note this doesn't include the 6 drinks we had at the bar waiting patiently. Just to put that into perspective, a similar order before they disappeared cost $40 (old place did not serve alcohol).

Listen Superiority Burger, I loved you, heck supported you during the worst times in the pandemic. When the rents went up 50%+ in the hood and I moved out, but I was determined to still support you. But the cost (seriously high cost means I'm socially guilted into tipping for bad service), awful wait times, the kludgey seating system. I won't be back for a very very very long time. Not until Christmas when I can use the bonus from my two jobs to afford it. There are much better vegetarian experiences in the city. Just like everything else in Manhattan, the wealthy ruined it.

Great news, it's as amazing as before. But even better now because plates! 

Long wait, duh. Grab a drink at the bodega next door and wait at the park, no big deal. 

Y'all mad it's expensive but do you want them to be open?? It's really great and worth it. The vibes are perfection. Have a great dinner!!!!

Superiority Burger is amazing. They've done a great job with the new spot and the new menu items are a hit. I was a huge fan of the collards on focaccia and the lentils. SO delicious! I'm excited to go back tonight.

The one-star reviews are just salty people. It's NYC, you wait for good food and pay the higher prices just as you did at the original location and as you do for any other restaurant. What's the point of writing a bad review for a newly opened restaurant that's still working out it's systems? If you have complaints, take it to the owner instead of the internet.

Superiority Burger

Spicy Lentils + Cornbread w/ Cabbage (Chunked, grilled, ramped)
- I enjoyed the texture of grilled cabbage in the soup-it added more character to it. The soup itself was really thick and surprisingly did have a kick of spiciness with perhaps peppercorn . 

Collard Greens Sandwich
Slow-Braised Collards, Cooper Sharp, our Focaccia
- The collards were well-seasoned, its greens not too soggy but stem cooked to al dente. 

Sloppy Dave
"On A Roll' with Frizzled Onion
- Sloppy Dave was my personal favorite. It reaffirms my belief that anything fried cannot taste bad. Only problem is that it is indeed sloppy, thus instead of holding it like a burger, I've had to use a folk and knife. The tomato sauce was a bit strongly seasoned to my taste but that is consistent with its fast-food theme. 

Specials: PB Pie
- The middle layer, I don't know what it was, was airy and made the sweet not too sweet, balancing out the peanut butter. PB pie was both savory and sweet, a good ending to the night. 

Food: Everything tasted good, and there was no single dish I was dissatisfied with. Not orworth, but great quality indeed. The wait time, however, was long--both waiting in line to get seated (it took us about an hour) and waiting for food. 
Price: Not super overpriced, considering the neighborhood, but the portion size for some dishes was kind of small.
Ambience: With white tiled-wall, some poems on the wall, and neon lights, it definitely has modern interior. Plus, its dim lights make it feel a little bit like a bar. 

 I would totally go back! I want to try different dishes but loved all the ones I've gotten. Hopefully, they start doing take-outs, since the wait time and price range is a bit steep.

Ugh, I just have such a bone to pick with this restaurant. Everything is on point -- the decor, the music, the service, the flavors -- everything. But the portion sizes are comically small. My party of three each ordered a burger and we got two shares for the table. The shares were well presented and delicious, as were the burgers, but were so smol it felt somewhat like a social experiment to have a tiny little half a sweet potato brought over to our table, the little plate nestled gently in the server's palms. Was it all a hoax? Was it a hidden camera prank show?? No, reader. Sadly, it was not. The half sweet potato to be shared by three adults was not a hoax. Nor was the adorable little cup of lentils with the square inch of cornbread. When the two tablespoons of PB&J pie was brought to our table (for which we paid fifteen American dollars), I wanted to chortle but had to exercise restraint. Even the delicious house soda I ordered was served in a tiny glass, mostly full of ice. As tasty as this meal was, I will not be returning to this restaurant.

Just to be clear, I am a long time fan of Superiority Burger. I love everything on their menu and would wait down the block on 9th street. I've gone twice to the new location and have been very disappointed, and really hope this might shed some light.

I don't think their current menu works for a sit down joint. Their meals are bite size, which was fine on Ninth street when you are expecting to get just a burger and go sit in the park but when you go sit down, I'm expecting a meal which is not what you're getting here. Last night, my date got his burger before I did, I insisted that he started eating because of how long we had been waiting for the table and he completed it before my sandwich had arrived. We both had a main dish, shared a side, a drink each and shared a desert and our bill totaled to $100 not including tip. We both left still hungry, had considered getting another side but after receiving the first beets side which arrived in a ketchup cup, decided against it. Would it make a difference and be filling? Didn't seem like it. As a vegetarian, I was pretty disappointed in not being satiated after choosing to go to sit down restaurants. Protein is already hard to come by, we at least need to have enough when we get it. 

I really hope they start doing take out. I love their food and wouldn't mind spending the money on a burger on a go, even knowing the size. It's not the prices that are a problem, their food is unique and worth it. I just don't have the patience to sit down after waiting over an hour for a table, order stacks of items and still not be full.

So happy they finally re-opened and our visit did not disappoint! We got there a few min before they opened and there was already a pretty long line. Luckily, the space is quite big and we were able to get seated on the first go. We shared a bunch of food between the three of us - Superiority burger, collard greens sandwich, roasted white sweet potato, campo rosso market salad, sweet & sour pink beets, spicy lentils + cornbread, and of course multiple desserts. Everything was on point - fresh and flavorful, with some unexpected combinations. We particularly loved the salad and were pleasantly surprised with the collard greens sandwich - def a MUST! The desserts were all delicious. I was so glad to finally have their sorbet again. Service was friendly and attentive at all times. As many others have mentioned, portions are small considering the prices, but they use high-quality and fresh seasonal ingredients, which you'll definitely taste.

A fun veggie/vegan restaurant in the colorful East Village. We had burgers and their unique and very tasteful collards on focaccia.  Super busy, but the service was excellent, and I plan to return there again.  It's hard to find another place that serves a collard sandwich.

This place is bangin' ! Take a trip back into the early 1980's with GREAT music and GREAT food. The veggie burger is off the charts and the inventive sides will keep your palette highly amused. Desserts are top notch/ aces. This is a vegetarian restaurant that also caters to vegans. I highly recommend this funky East Village fun place. Staff is highly engaged and professional.

Long-time fan of Superiority Burger.  It was great as a small snack-bar takeout spot, but does not translate well into a sit-down restaurant.  The eponymous burger can be eaten in about 30 seconds, so they should adjust the menu/portion sizes to be more consistent with a sit-down restaurant.  Had the burger, two sides and the sorbet...all very good but still pretty much exactly as they were in the old location.

A long-time fan of SB and this new spot exceeded all expectations. The food is outrageously delicious and comforting. The cocktails are excellent. Service is great and staff are super friendly. Music is a twisted blend of punk and couldn't be better. They just opened so it's very difficult to get a table, and no reservations, no take-out, but do not let that put you off. We love going every weekend, putting our name down then killing time at Mast Books and sipping cocktails in the back bar. Best items: ALL OF THEM. But seriously, try the Yuba and indulge in a dessert.

I had been to Superiority Burger before the pandemic when they were just a hole in the wall establishment but when I heard they had moved into a bigger location, I needed to try it again! We decided to go when we heard there would be a pop up by Bakers Bench (Vegan croissants?! Yes please!) We got there a little after 5 and it was already pretty packed!
Really liked the diner type set up. The tables are pretty close together but there is still room to navigate the place. Now, onto the food! Their burgers were always a good choice, but I decided to try something new and ordered the white sweet potato. It was pretty filling! My friend who I was with had never been there before so she ordered the superiority burger vegan. We were also able to order the pop up items while at our table and they were added to our final bill. 
Note: I rated 4 stars because they took my coffee from me as I entered the restaurant. I know this is really on me, but I hadn't had that happen in a while. Also, considering it was Pride weekend they could have assumed it could have contained alcohol. Another note: they do have a liquor license so if you're in the mood for a cocktail, they looked good!

It's a vegetarian place so that's great! We ordered the house soda, superiority burger, sloppy Joe, broccoli salad, which was my favorite, spicy lentils, tasty yuba verde and stuffed cabbage. The spicy lentils and broccoli salad was tasty! Yuba verde was too bland and it was 19$ for a very small portion of bread and some veggies. the sandwiches needed some hot sauce. To me everything was overpriced. It was almost tapas size, not what you expect when you go to a burger place and the soda was $10, while it was tasty and not sweet it was a small glass and really overpriced. So the food is tasty but to me not worth the $$$$ and the 1.15 hour long wait.

My roommate and I put our names down at 5pm and waited an hour for a table on a Saturday night. Well worth the wait! I don't have words for the superiority burger. The patty is so smoky and delicious, and the bread is soft and buttery. The collard greens sandwich was an adventurous choice for us but was also very flavorful, especially because of the focaccia. We also had the date shake and the funnel cake, both of which were incredible. The desserts were mouth watering without being too sweet, which is a rare feat. I definitely will be returning to try other sandwiches - and order that date shake again.

So great to have Superiority back in the neighborhood, and in the iconic Odessa space no less. The food was fantastic as always, with the old classics back and some new tasty items as well. The service is chill but attentive, and there seems to be a huge number of people on staff running around at all times in the new much bigger space. The throwback menus and nostalgic touches all around recognize the history of the space and the neighborhood. One small note - no need to have people "wait at the bar" for 5-10 minutes in the hope that they buy a cocktail while waiting, while there are lots of seats quite apparently available. We'll happily order drinks when we sit down because they're delicious!

Superiority has grown up and has become a great addition to the East Village sit down restaurant scene, and one of the few late night options remaining here.

had a really disappointing and baffling meal here the other night. what they have on their menu as "beans and pasta" is a essentially a minuscule cup of black bean soup. it was $15. the baked japanese sweet potato, also $15 was a quarter (if that) of a single roasted potato served with chopped up pickles, labneh and a barely detectable green sauce. the flavor was fine, i guess, but the precious portion felt totally confused and honestly rude. we also had the plate of veggies, which was so completely nothing it's hard to believe it wasn't just presented for free at the start of our meal. it consisted of a few steamed and raw veggies and was served with a tofutti-like dip that was too dense and didn't have much flavor and a side of very hot sauce, which was enjoyable and maybe my favorite thing from the entire meal. the lentils had nice flavor and the 1x1 inch cube of cornbread it came with was good, but again the portion and pricing for pureed lentils totally baffled all of us at the table. i'd had the burger a few years ago and thought it was fine; it's still fine. it doesn't come with fries, which is hateful in my opinion. i sadly don't have a single nice thing to say about the sloppy joe, which we all agreed was just plain whack, and the $21 green yuba sandwich was fine/hardly a noteworthy sandwich. the black sesame gelato was delicious, but it was $11 for a tiny scoop. you can get a fresh pint of delicious vegan ice cream from van leuwen for $13. i wanted to like this place because i'd heard good things, but given the prices our meal felt completely inadequate and wholly unsatisfying.

i was genuinely excited to try this place now that they graduated from the small storefront that used to exist on my street a few months ago, however things took a turn as soon as we stepped in to inquire about the wait.

upon entering there was a couple in front of us also checking about the wait, the hostess (idk her name, but the white girl with glasses) was being very rude about them leaving the restaurant to wait for their table. we got up there and were told a little over an hour for a table (fine okay no problem, we live in the area anyways) and so we went to grab drinks nearby. it's been well over the time so we come back  and she asks us the name on the waitlist, we say it but she doesn't hear us so i say the name a little louder (mind you it's very loud in the restaurant) and she makes the ugliest face imaginable and condescendingly says "suuupperrrrrr" and says our table isn't ready (again, no problem!) and that we can wait at the bar in the back.....there's a bar in the back and she didn't think to mention it before we went off to look for one ourself (the bar isn't really visible from the front so there's no way we would have seen it)....anyways!! 

we sit down, the food was "okay", i liked my partners dish more and he liked mine more so we ended up switching. the girl serving us was sweet and lovely but the service overall is a shit show (again, not the end of the world but not a good look for a new restaurant).

please do yourself a favor and hire better front of house staff, that hostess was unnecessarily rude and nasty to most of the people walking through. if you can't see that then you're truly not paying enough attention.

The food is good.I would not say amazing - the portions are kind of insulting and the prices are high.   Each dish is portioned like a side. It's basically vegan tapas. Odessa was place that kept people well fed at a good price - sad that the east village lost that for this

Superiority Burger has the vibe and ambiance of an old school diner. The menu features a few interesting meatless sandwiches and burgers and sides. I had the Yuba Verde sandwich and then shared the lentils (with cornbread) and the fried eggplant and white sweet potato. The portion sizes are pretty small for the price you pay, but the food was tasty. Luckily, I only had a 15 minute wait when I went on a Thursday evening. The yurba verde sandwich had tofu skin and broccoli rabe on a baguette. My friends also got the funnel cake dessert, which was more like a thick, soft fried doughnut with berries and ice cream. Overall, I would go again but be prepared to spend more $$$ than you think!

Was there this past weekend and could not have been more pleased.

The ambience was very upbeat, from the maitre d' to the server (Colleen).  And, boy, did it feel good to see Brooks there, bussing tables, serving, and keeping an eye on everything going on.  

We arrived around 5:45 and had expected to wait a long time, but we were told it would be 30-45 min and she was right on the money.  We waited on benches in TSP and the time flew.  Got the text, crossed the street, and got seated.  

The diner vibe was fun and felt authentic.

As for the food, my partner and I shared 2 entrees.  Let's start w/ the burger.  It wasn't the biggest burger I'd ever seen, but that's perfectly OK.  Size doesn't matter.  It was cooked great, dressed very well, and a joy to eat!  The difficulty eating it was that the knowledge that it wouldn't last forever - that there would be a last bite, and then I'd be done. 

We had both expected the burger to be the star of the show (the diner is named after it after all), but, while it was a star of the show, it wasn't the brightest star.  I'm not putting it down (I could live on only SBs for a few decades, I'm sure), but the collard greens sandwich was crazy delish.  I'm a greens fan, and I like veg food, so we thought it would be good, but eating it required us both to pace ourselves.  It would be done, but we didn't want to think about a time when we didn't have a collard greens sandwich in front of us.  We're still talking about it.

And, as for the portion size, when the entrees got served, I remember thinking, "kinda small."  I mentioned to my partner that if we're still hungry when we'll have finished our entrees, maybe we'll order of stuff cabbage and split it.  Not at all necessary.  By the time we (we're slow eaters) finished, we were fully sated.  If the portions had been bigger, we might have been uncomfortable, but we weren't; we were full but not too full.

The prices?  I hope they can stay in business with prices that low.  All told, food, tax, tip came to $55 for the 2 of us for a meal (and service) that blew our minds.  I had a hard cider w/ my meal, also, and that was pleasant and priced right.

One more thing.  Maybe 2.

The recipe for the burger is online!  It's crazy.  He's not only offering it in his diner, but he's giving it away, if you want to make it yourself!  Brooks Headley is living in a world I want to be part of.  Seriously.  He's competent and generous - what a combo!

Also, the vibe (as evidenced by the language used in the menu and the various signs posted) are soooo positive.  When he says stuff isn't available (and it's nice that he says so, so that expectations can be managed), he doesn't say it's not available.  He says it's not available yet, or now.  Wait a little and it might be back, or, they'll get to it, but not at the moment.  

I guess it made a strong positive impression on me.  We'll be back, but next time we'll bring friends (so we can try more things on the menu).

Hats off to Brooks! (a little joke, cause he's a paper hat wearer). See you again, and I hope it's soon!!

This place is not worth the hype. The burger itself is pretty tasty--not amazing but very good--but it's tiny, come with no sides, and costs $14. I probably could have eaten three of them. 

They don't have fries on the menu and the sides are just tiny little tapas. For drinks, there are no special or creative cocktails, just basic ones you might have found in 1960 in a diner. I guess that's "authentic" but like to what end?

In the end, we left hungry and wondering why we spent an hour waiting for a table. If this were a fast food place with no wait, I'd probably come back. As a a sit-down place with a perennial wait, it's just not worth the time or money.

The Superiority Burger has more umami than Umami Burger, and it's deliciously plant-based. This place came highly recommended to me, and it delivered. A burger worth savoring. The aesthetics in here allude to old school diners and old school punk rock with a hint of tiki culture at the bar (or did I imagine that?). Dig the photocopied menus with odd bits like Morrissey's teenage negative review of the Ramones (he'll never live that down). I even heard the Circle Jerks "Back Against the Wall" in the eclectic music mix of funk, soul, and whatnot. I couldn't get the hang of the Coca-Cola with salted peanuts. I am proud of myself for trying, but I believe it's supposed to be served with shelled peanuts, not peanuts in the shell. If you're in NYC, do not miss this place.

It's pretty crazy to see any bad reviews on here, if I lived in the neighborhood I'd eat here every day. Food was just absolutely incredible, so creative and SO flavorful, just a wild surprising ride all the way through. The desserts were absolutely mindblowing. And the service was SO friendly from the door to the table, there were probably 3 different people who helped serve us and they were all friendly and helpful even when we were being wish washy about choosing from a rollercoaster of a menu. 

Will return to eat everything I didn't eat the first time.

It's busy, but it's not as it used to be. The wait is long. The servers are rushed. Good portions are small. But everything was tasty. 

Dessert is better than anything I had on the real menu. We got one of everything for dessert and agreed it was better than their meals.

This place used to be my favorite.. 

Way more expensive now but with Smaller portions.  one special (some peppers and couple pieces of  tiny fried tofu) before 12 midnight was over 20 bucks plus tax / tip, which left me hungry as it was on the smaller side barely enough for a single person..  

Had to wait  till midnight to order again & pay another 16 bucks for a Tft which was lukewarm. 

Unfortunately, could not get gelato/sorbet even though I saw the staff keep some aside etc.   

About 40+ bucks for 2 things (single person) without any soft beverage or desserts.. Service was mediocre.   

Will give it another shot but NYC has much more to offer in the same price range.

I love Superiority Burger! As a vegetarian, it's amazing to find a diet friendly place that has a cool vibe and ever changing specials that introduce you to new flavors. The burgers are a must have, but also so is the hippy poutine! I've never had a homemade ice cream sandwich with jam until SB, and I cannot stop thinking about it. The house soda is always interesting as well. The Night Shift is the best for late night bites.

Overall: 3.5/5 stars

I went with my friend on a Thursday night. It took us about 20 minutes to be seated. The server was so nice and remembered what we wanted for dessert.

For food, the fried eggplant was a standout, followed by the broccoli salad. Everything was seasoned well. The desserts were exceptional!

The atmosphere is super cute and casual! A little pricey overall, but worth a try.

Amazing! I am not a vegetarian but this food was so so good. Our server was awesome. We got there before 5 and once they opened we were able to get a table right away. The cocktails were also outstanding - I had my favorite, an Aperol Spritz, but they had some more unique concoctions to choose from as well. Try as much as you can, there was nothing I did not like. The burger was outstanding. A big surprise favorite of mine was the collard greens sandwich. I'm from the South, the land of collard greens at Sunday supper. My sister ordered it and the focaccia - holy bread. Crispy, nutty, warm. The collards were not bitter at all, very savory with the perfect pairing of a salty cheese. For dessert- several great items to choose from but we chose the Finn's cake and it didn't disappoint. Warm and crispy with the best gelato on top. The inside of this restaurant has a great vibe, buzzing and happy employees and diners. This place is a must for any foodie.

Avant Garden, LadyBird, and Superiority Burger are all located within 500 feet of each other. I had dined at both Avant Garden and Ladybird in the past.

I decided to give Superiority Burger a try, but I was very disappointed. The Superiority Burger was just okay, and let's just say that the collard green sandwich is an acquired taste. Additionally, the hostess was blatantly rude and offensive.

That said, the sorbet at Superiority Burger is fantastic, but I won't be setting foot in there again.

If you're looking for great vegan food and a pleasant ambiance, you can't go wrong with either Avant Garden or LadyBird.

Avant Garden's Artichoke and Risotto dish is to die for, and Ladybird's Eggplant and KFB are mouthwateringly delicious.

Like Action Bronson says F... That's Delicious. 

I came by for a quick dinner and was blown away. The host quoted 30ish wait which I assumed there would be - but by the time I walked to a bench in Tompkins my table was ready. Or more like a seat at the counter. Love it, quick and easy. 
The place is much bigger than I expected and it was packed both in dining section and at the bar in the back. The decor is of a classic old school diner. Photos, bags, posters on the wall. 
It's not cheap and solo dinner was $50. But I'd say it's truly worth it.
/ Collard Greens Sandwich 10/10!!! Perfectly toasted focaccia with gooey rich collard greens. I usually sit finish bread on sandwiches but on this one the plate was clean. 
/ AL's NA beer 10/10 Anyone who offers NA drink menu is MVP in my book. One of the best tasting non alcoholic beers I've had. And for $5.50 (side eye to all restaurants charging $10-20 for flavored water lol)
/ SB Banana Bread 10/10! Wowie, warm banana square with coconut ice cream and chocolate olive oil and pecan. Ice cream isn't too strong of coconut and whatever is in that banana bread is crack. Not too sweet. Perfect way to end the meal. 

Service is excellent. Attentive and fast. I had a great meal and was on my way. Will be back!

AND adding to my Best of East Village collection.

It's everything  you have heard-delicious, cute (dark) diner atmosphere, amazing vegetarian and vegan choices. Pricey, but I'll go again. Super casual. Get there 15 min before it opens to be guaranteed a first seating. Ideal to go on a weeknight, NOT weekend.

Great ambience of a classic diner, but with vegan ingredients. The burger is pretty good, but overall I felt the food was a little overhyped. Could have done with a few more flavorings and toppings. The spinach spanakopita style sandwich was OK but a bit bland.

Also disappointed that almost all the beers were canned, not draft. Wait times for service can be a little long too. Overall, it was good but you can definitely find better vegan food in this price range.
This place is a vibe! The menu is amazing. I'm not vegan, but every item I tried was insane! I will be coming back time and time again.

Waited for about an hour for a table for 2 around 7 on a Saturday. You can't get a reservation here so go early and put your name down and go to a nearby bar (we waited at Lovers of Today and it was great!). Once we were seated, the food came out pretty quickly. Here's what we got: 

Burnt Broccoli Salad - this was not my cup of tea. They don't provide ingredients on their menu which is frustrating because there was a flavor in here (not sure what) but it was really overpowering for my taste. I know this is one of the most popular things here but I was not a fan. 

Sloppy Dave - this was also just ok. The burger came out really really soggy which was kind of off putting. The actual filling was ok, kind of bland/not much going on. I wouldn't get this. Our waitress recommended the Yuba Verde and our neighbors got it and said it was fantastic so wish we got that instead.

Superiority Burger - this was probably the best thing we got, though a bit on the dry side so would ask for more sauces on the side. Very good flavor, soft buns, definitely get this if you come here. 

Griddled Malt Cake - This was ok as well. Coconut cake with cream cheese gelato. The cake itself was ok in my opinion but the gelato was really good! Wish I could just get a scoop of that on the side. 

Choco Haupia Pie - My favorite dessert of the two! Basically chocolate mudpie with a hint of coconut. Definitely good for people like me who like chocolate in their desserts!

Overall, this place was on the pricey side and very average, nothing out of this world or mindblowingly tasty. If I were to come next time, I would probably just try more of the sides and maybe dessert.

Inventive combinations of plant based food.

Friendly service, and we were able to get a table without a wait?  Admittedly that was a surprise and others were not so lucky.

Really enjoyed the burger.  Why no fries?  Who knows.

Unfortunately they are an ableist establishment when it comes to the noise level, which is mostly a function of them choosing to blast the background music.  One person in our party has a hearing challenge and this made it particularly challenging. 85db is the average level of a movie in a movie theater.....way too loud for a place people are supposed to be able to communicate and interact.
Amazing food.  Cool diner theme.  Waitress was very helpful and made excellent recommendations.

Call me a 2nd-wave Superiority Burger eater as I've eaten many more meals now at the current, new location over the former, original spot on 9th Street. The staff are super sweet and patient with providing updates on waiting time; every waiter has a friendly and unique personality, willing to have a convo when able! While I miss the classic Odessa decorations, SB has maintained the look and inserted more memories of the East Village with relevant and exciting decorations and posters including an advertisement flier from See Hear, a former zine shop around the corner, or personal photographs of former vegan restaurants (i.e. Dojo) and punk bands of the neighborhood.

While I've enjoyed just about every meal I've had since they opened, I don't think I've ever had a better waffle than the one I ate yesterday, on their second day of offering lunch service. Served with syrup and creamy guava butter, I didn't want the waffle to go cold so ate probably too quickly. I topped it off with a classic, megamouth burger and the lunch tray-- served with a notably amazing pineapple and apple cider desert, and focaccia cinnamon bun. I cannot wait for what they introduce next. RIP Odessa, but the spot has a bright future with a new host.

I heard about Superiority Burger before I moved to the city, and was excited to see that it reopened after shuttering for over a year. 

The ambiance is interesting. There are references to other businesses around town and old newspaper ads for decor. They were playing audio of announcements from a Japanese train station in the bathroom. Definitely quirky.

I had the superiority burger and a side of lentils and cornbread. Both the burger patty and the lentils had a rich blend of spices and a little bit of heat. Both were definitely tasty. However, the portions were quite small, and the bill came out to over $40 after tax and tip. After waiting so long, I really wanted to love this place, but it's just way too expensive.

The space and ambiance are great, although my watch actually warned me about the noise levels. (!) The service was basically good. 

The food was delicious.

But . . . there wasn't enough of it! Especially at these prices. 

The menu says the superiority burger, now $17.00, is "megamouth size" but it's not that much bigger than the old one was. 

The server mentioned potato soup as a special and my friend ordered it, thinking she was getting a bowl, but got what can only be described as a cup . . . for $10.00. She was very unhappy. 

I'd seen the menu before going, and expected the prices, but I also expected much more food than we got. Calling this small burger "megamouth" size is unrealistic, and the failure to mention the tiny soup size left my friend hungry - she had to order a wrap afterward from a place a couple of blocks away. The server should have mentioned the soup was so small, especially since that was all she got. 

When superiority burgers were $6.00 I couldn't get enough and often stopped by and grabbed a couple. But $17? No.

This place needs no introduction as there was a decent crowd waiting for the doors to open on a Sunday evening. We got seated in a booth and were promptly welcomed by the friendly waitress. Naturally, we got two of the classic burgers and a side of Brocolli w hummus , as well as a tasty salad.
We really enjoyed all the food and probably could have eaten two of the burgers each. They were a little more mushy than the ones I make at home and I feel a little bit of extra Chris Ping would have been a nice contrast.

There is a bar in the back, and and a good selection of drinks and cocktails. The restaurant lived up to its reputation. 
It was casual, cool diner vibe, friendly, unrushed, dinner w all vegan entries.

Shame on this spot - and the New York Times for writing it up. The $17 vegetarian burger is one of the worst such burgers in the city - the entire menu is overpriced and subpar. Absolutely overhyped but below the line of any comparable restaurant which makes it so disappointing - not worth the time or money. The toilet however is top notch (extra star!)

Also - do folks just have low standards? Everyone here is reporting the same: poor food, poor value, but leaving 3+ stars.

it's a lil cute and funny spot...
the menu is unexpected and remains so over the years
if ur walking around ev and want an imaginative snack or jus rly gud ice cream come here

I went to Superiority Burger last Thursday and expected there to be a long line. We came on the earlier end (around 5:30) so there were actually a lot of tables open and were able to be seated immediately. In order to be seated, the entire party has to be present, which is important especially since you can't make reservations ahead of time. 

The service was pretty quick once we sat down, so we first ordered our appetizers: the burnt broccoli salad and the halloumi and beans (forgot the name of this dish but it's new). Both appetizers were pretty good but not outstanding. For my main, I obviously had to get the Superiority Burger, which was great, but pretty minimal for $17. It doesn't come with any sides or anything else so plating-wise does look pretty barren. That being said, it is a great vegetarian burger and you can taste the quality of the ingredients, so I also can understand the price. 

If you come to this restaurant, you also have to get dessert. If you're not super hungry, I would skip the appetizers and just get a burger and dessert. We ordered the banana bread, the ice cream cake, and the chocolate fudge cake. The chocolate cake came with a delicious ice cream covered in crunchy caramel and the banana bread was amazing. The portions are on the smaller side so you can share a few but they're also pretty decadent.
Delicious meatless food. Portion was small for price. Beets and burger was flavorful and delicious. Broccoli wasn't bad as well

Solid veggie burgers and good vibes.

I had known of Superiority Burger for years, but I have no idea from where or why. However, shortly after moving to New York I was hungry on a Saturday evening and realized this place was nearby, so my friend and I stopped by.

At 5:30 pm it was already buzzing, but we were able to be seated instantly. I'm not sure if there was a wait further in the evening, but for the duration of our meal it seemed like all the tables were taken.

My friend and I each got our own superiority burger, and we split the burnt broccoli. The sauce on the broccoli was interesting, but I think it got old after a few bites to be honest (and it was a MOUND of broccoli). The burger meanwhile was very tasty-- I appreciate the option of vegan cheese or not.

I loved how they described each of the cocktails as a chair on their placemat. It makes for great conversation fodder as you wait for your food.

Service was fast and friendly. All in all a solid spot, but I think the sides seem a little bit like a miss. Also note: they don't serve fries :(
Portions and prices aside, SB is still one of the best food out there. Their brunch menu is truly amazing and please, do yourself a favor and get the dates shake.
The desserts!!! Still dreaming about the banana bread, and loved the chocolate mousse cake

Finally made it to the new location (twice now).  I'd eat here at least once a week if I lived or worked closer.  

This is everything food (and especially vegetarian food) should be.  It's real ingredients (no fake processed faux meat), and crave-able, flavorful dishes.  And menu items change regularly, so there is always something new to try! 

We opted to try some of the new menu items instead of the burger, which we have already had.  I can't choose a favorite - the beans w/ pasta was so good, I'll order whatever "beans and.." combination is on the menu next time.  It was hearty without being heavy. Crispy eggplant was delightful in texture and taste.  Collards sandwich was savory on a fluffy and crisp piece of focaccia.  

Service was great, and the retro diner vibe is very fun and fits perfectly in the neighborhood.  I know there is often a long wait, so suggest planning to put your name down and have a drink while you wait at one of the many bars close by. 

Probably goes without saying, but I'd recommend this restaurant to anyone and everyone.

It has been years since I've gone out to dinner and felt actively angry... I've been vegan for three years and the idea that paying 17$ for a pathetic veggie burger with no fries and a weak piece of lettuce in the middle is what is marketed as a full meal is the biggest rip off I've ever seen in my entire life. Really actively disgusting.

We enjoyed this, even if we don't totally understand the hype. We loved the marcella beans with escarole/halloumi/jalopenos. I really liked the spicy lentils with cornbread, but it was a little bit too heavy for my wife. We both thought the sweet potato was great. The superiority burger and the collards sandwich were both very good. We both really enjoyed the chocolate peppermint cake for dessert.

Making my return to Yelp to do Superiority Burger the justice it deserves. Lot's of people are claiming it's overhyped (due to Tik Tok brain rot), but I'm here to set the record straight. If you're a vegetarian or vegan, you know that since the invention of the beyond burger, it's been almost impossible to find a decent veggie burger that isn't some sort of contrived fake meat imitation. Has it ever occurred to burger joints that some vegetarians don't particularly like or want meat, much less an uncanny imitation of it?

Anyways, Superiority Burger's namesake dish is an honest to god bean burger, and a delicious one at that. Next time I'm craving a burger I'll gladly pay double what it might cost me at *** ***** Burger if it means I don't have to eat impossible meat

superiority burger has an inferiority complex. the staff that served us were not welcoming. they made my friends and I feel like we were inconveniencing them by asking to be seated and served. the food was fine, but not worth the price point ($17 for just a burger). overall, the experience went against the atmosphere i believe the establishment is trying to achieve - casual cool, laidback, and scrappy. instead, it was uptight and snobby. i am truly confused by the hype.

I dined at the restaurant based on reviews I read in Eater NY and NYT. I am sorry to say that the praised vege burger was a huge disappointment. Small dried out patty. Advertised as a "mega mouth " burger. It was more like a slider. I was hungry after I left. I have had better veggie burgers at diners. Service was pleasant at least.

Don't believe the hype. 

There are far better options for vegetarian/vegan food in the city. If you're looking for a reliably good veggie burger, go to byChloe or Peace Food Cafe. 

The portions are small. The prices aren't cheap. The food is mediocre. We tried the superiority burger which tasted as if someone had sloppily assembled a burger using a dr.praeger's frozen veggie patty and other leftover ingredients. The date shake is also too sweet. 

The only redeeming qualities are its cozy diner ambiance and prompt service. We were in and out in 45 minutes.

I hope the owners use the recent attention as an opportunity to reinvest in and focus on its food. If not, I don't think they'll last.

Superiority Burger has long been one of my favorite places to eat; when their home was a tiny storefront on 9th street, we would queue around the block for amazing taste treats. Now that Brooks Headley--one of the owners--has occupied the longtime space of the Odessa, a Ukrainian diner on Avenue A, he has more options and also: a liquor license!

I generally wear my earplugs in this place, because I have hearing loss and don't want it to get worse. SB reminds me strongly of another favorite diner of mine in the 80s: 103 Second avenue, at Second Avenue and Sixth street. They had a jukebox, and the vibe is the same. (103 was 24 hours.) 

I can't afford to eat here often, but I have appreciated when they've expanded their hours. They have hosted--ooh! aah!--celebrity guests in their curtained-off back room, and they are already a staple of the neighborhood.

Just went for the third time and I guess three's not a charm in that after an hour wait and trying some new things on the menu I will not be returning. The burger and collard greens sandwich are always good but we couldn't figure out if the burnt broccoli with coriander dressing tasted like a musty house or just plain ashes. The Sloppy Dave sandwich was too sweet and gloppy and lukewarm at that.
Then, while lingering a bit to drink our water after paying the bill,  a waitperson
asked if we wanted anything else so I asked her if she wanted us to leave and without hesitation or a smile she said yes.

My favorite restaurant in the city.  The way the menu experiments with available ingredients and textures is breathtaking.  The stuffed cabbage and TFTs and any soup they may have are must trys.  The market salad is also great.  And don't sleep on the desserts and that amazing snack mix by the bar.  The service is also always great and the vibes are fabulous.

I finally made it out to to try some of their brunch items and honestly, just thinking about this post has me hungry to return.

Highly recommend everything we got to share between the two of us:
- Chuck Bettis Breakfast 'Chorizo' sandwich. So flavorful, you wouldn't even realize this is vegetarian.

- Idaho Spud Hashbrowns: the perfect texture and mix of crunch and saucy. My only gripe is that I wanted more! The portion size was a bit small but maybe that's because I shared it 

- Waffle with Guava Butter. This was such an interesting texture that I wasn't expecting. It was super crunchy and (fried?) but was absolutely addictive.

I love the diner atmosphere and will absolutely be back soon.

4.8/5

Eh. After loving the original, this new version was pretty disappointing. It's a cool space and the food is fresh, but that's where the positives end. You feel incredibly rushed there (servers literally grab your plate while your last bite is still in your mouth), and a bit ripped off. Possibly my fav sandwich in the whole world was "The New Creation" with yuba skin at the old SB, so I was really excited to try the Yuba Verde sandwich here. Unfortunately it was 90 percent broccoli rabe. The rabe was very good, but $23 for a broccoli rabe sandwich? You couldn't taste the yuba at all. Overall the magic in the food (every little detail down to the buns used to be perfect) that was once there is now gone. So combined with the price, it just didn't feel worth it. Oh well. It was great while it lasted.

this place is just so expensive for what it is. It's just living off the hype of the original location, which only had hype to begin with because its prices were accessible. But the burger that was once $6 is now $17 and in that time period inflation hasn't been 300%, and you're paying tip now so the $17 sandwich post tax/tip is now $22... instead of $6.50.

The small pie slices are $15... the basic cocktails (negroni, old fashioned) are $17... this is empire has no clothes fake accessible. Like if people keep telling us it's a down to earth diner, maybe we'll believe them. The food is good but there's nothing special about it, even if you're vegetarian. At this price point, go somewhere a bit more ambitious and memorable.

Ok...this spot is definitely delicious. But if you're looking for like...an inventive vegan burger, this isn't it. If you're looking for really delicious vegan food--then you've found it. Its giving high end, punk diner vibes with some inventive plates on the menu. But the burger? Basic, well-made, kinda boring.

This was a very disappointing experience. The space is great and I admit I do miss Odessa. But I held out hope Superiority Burger would live up to the hype. The food was just bad. Nothing was well-seasoned and it was bland. The portions were also small and very pricey for what it was. Another small quibble is the presentation. That plates are too small and left little room what they did serve.
believe the hype!!! very empty at 6 on a monday, not too loud and service was quick. LOVEEE
Believe the hype. Wow. The sloppy Joe is indeed sloppy but incredibly tasty. The burger texture is perfect

Stumbled upon the new restaurant post an exhibition nearby. We were a group of 9 - 4 adults and 5 children and decided to try the restaurant for a quick bite. 

We checked in and indicated we were a large group. The hostess was a bit apprehensive about the size but I said we were willing to split up to two different tables with different checks or even one check, what ever was easy for them. She said she had to speak to the manager who then came out and said sorry they could not accommodate as there were just too many children. I pointed out what if we were to separate families walking in - would she have declined? She kept coming up with different excuses and in the end I pointed out the restaurant was just not very family friendly. At that point she relented and sat us down in two separate tables at two opposites ends of the restaurant. 

We ordered the burger and waffles - as did the other table. The food was pretty yummy albeit smaller portions. The service once seated was also good and prompt. 

Would have given more rating for this place had the service at check in been better, especially for large groups / families.
good spot nice burger excellent sides will go back although it is loud but a great location

The music was too loud. That's really the only bad thing I can say about our experience at Superiority Burger. Everything else was simply excellent. I can't even justify knocking off a star for the noise because the food was delicious. I had the superiority burger -- amazing. Husband got the "sloppy Dave." We shared the beets, which were nothing like I expected -- just an incredible combination of flavor and texture (fried pretzels?!). For dessert, he had the banana bread, which he proclaimed the best dessert he'd ever had. (And the man eats a lot of desserts.) I got two of the ice creams: the red pear sorbet and the blue corn gelato. I ate all of it (and I am not a big dessert eater). I want to go back tomorrow so I can get the collard green sandwich and try more of the sides and desserts. Up there with my favorite meals I've had in the city.

What is this?! Why is it so hyped up?! Is it the desserts? Ok maybe, but you REALLY can't justify paying $20 for tiny sandwiches that aren't even organic. Why are people so entranced to pay $17 for some tofu skin? It's obviously a cult for morons!

The food sounded good on paper, but was very meh irl (overwhelmingly vinegary soup, undercooked sweet potato, and incredibly sweet dessert). The verde sandwich was good, but not worth $25. Wouldn't recommend, unfortunately :(

I am not a vegetarian and quite frankly thought that Superiority Burger was all hype. While I hate to admit it, I couldn't have been more wrong. The food at Superiority Burger is delicious and creative. The burger is outstanding. The service is excellent. The cocktails and wine are great too. Also, it is a real bargain. The space is a pleasant reminder of an older time, but with updated design elements too. If you are a vegetarian you have to go. If you are a carnivore you have to go. Superiority Burger is terrific.

We thought it was good burger place, so we decided to try. 
Superiority burger was small, not special at all, not tasty, and  the bun was cheap, horrible puffy thing. 
The coconuts soup was OK but small bowl for $15?? Not worth it.
Odessa was great, but this cheap Diner looking place charges cheap cocktail $17!  The quality is not even real bar level, asking for real $. 
We don't understand why people come here
We will never come back here

Finally ate here tonight.  Sat at the bar, it was crowded.  I got the burger which is $18.  Basically it's a black bean burger which surprised me because those were popular in the late 90s yet it's 2024.  Burger was ok but definitely not worth $18.  The lady serving me was nice and the burger came out quickly.  Coffee was actually good.  Still I thought the burger would be more creative.

My gut told me to order the collard greens sandwich so I will go back and try that and update my review of it knocks my socks off.

Came for brunch. I suspect that the positive reviews were all for dinner because brunch was a SERIOUS miss.

Positives: yes, the burger is good. Is it $18 good? No, it is not. It is a small 3 inch thin patty with more lettuce than burger. If you want a side you'll shell out $13 for hashbrowns which were pathetically small. Bread plate size; SMALL bread plate size.

The $16 shake? It was oddly salty and came in a 4 ounce water glass. Come on, you jest? Nope. No I don't. 4 ounce water glass. It was embarrassing.

Am I now going to shell out $18 for a slice of pie? You know, fool me once, shame on you...we stopped there. Got the check and made it in time to line up for donuts at Wild Air which helped restore my faith in restaurant humanity.

This was so underwhelming. I expect dinner is better but if this is the best they got for brunch? Hard pass.
4 people, 300 dollars, hipster pretentious, small portions, boring burger, never again!

$50 + tip for two sandwiches.
No exaggeration.
No fries, extras, sides, nothing. 
I eat at restaurants often--this is egregiously overpriced.

I wouldn't mind but the bartender in the back who took our order was such a rude jerk I had to come write a review. He threw our bag of food at us and stormed away despite having received a handsome tip for doing nothing beyond entering our basic 2 item takeaway order into the system. There wasn't even anyone at the bar he had to tend to. It wasn't busy or packed. Just a jerk for no reason. Honestly ruined my evening.

For what it's worth its a solid vegan burger. The yuba verde sandwich was also solid tasting. Neither worth a quarter of a hundred bucks. Ambiance certainly didn't make up for it.

I've eaten here a handful of times. 

The first few visits were ok, once I/my party was actually seated. The younger of the two people at the host station in the front always gave an immense attitude, and either never entered my information in for the wait list, or gave preference to other patrons. 

I/the people I went to SB with have worked in service before and are understanding that sometimes things happen, but after the third instance of seating not being available, even sometimes a half an hour or more after the estimated wait time we all started to wonder what the deal was. These were not overly busy times.

The attitude served by the host when politely checking in after the estimated wait time should have been enough to make any of us never want to support this place but fond memories of the OG SB and the desire to support a punk owned business kept us there. 

Add this to the list of reviews with an issue about SB's pricing...despite enjoying the food the first few times (burger, lentils, salad) it was hard to ignore the fact that none of us were satisfied, nor could we justify ordering more to keep from being hungry. 

While I appreciate the use of premium produce and other ingredients, I'm sorry to say that the food doesn't do it justice. 

The last couple of times the texture of the burger wasn't great.

The final straw was when I went in on a slow rainy weeknight and the aforementioned host said it would be just a few minutes for a seat. I was told to go sit at the bar in the back, when I declined (I don't drink and don't want to be in that environment) and asked if I could wait in the front (there was no one else there) I was told very aggressively to sit at the bar. 

I left.
Didn't know this was vegetarian when we went, but boy were we blown away! Tried the hash browns which were a 7/10 and the boysenberry pie was a 11/10 so cute inside as well

I went several weeks ago. But I will never in my life that collard green focaccia sandwich. DAMN it was good.

Hip. Bit of a wait. Expectations were managed well and with the appropriate level of sass.

Tried to sweet-talk my way into an early fried tofu sandwich. It didn't work. They're not ready until they're ready, people.

I've been meaning to check out this place for a while, and it did not disappoint! The whole vibe is VERY cool, the lighting makes everything seem fun, and our waiter was lovely. I had the sloppy dave, which is a LOT of very messy food, though the mess is very much worth it. Will definitely have to try the Superiority Burger next time. I also had the ice cream for desert, which was lovely and refreshing, and wasn't TOO much ice cream, which I appreciated.

A hip concept for vegetarian eats -- they're set up like a classic diner and serve up burgers and more! The vibes were really nice and it was pretty packed on a weekday evening, which should give you an idea of how popular it is. I got the Yuba-Verde sandwich and it was really unique -- the broccoli texture threw me off a bit and the bread got soggy. I'm convinced that I didn't get my favorite thing on the menu, but I'd definitely come back to give it a try!

The ambiance is great, good music selection, fine job at preserving the integrity of the storied Odessa diner, which was one of my favorites. Although the food was good, the portions are shockingly small, and the price incredibly steep for what you get. I never went to the old Superiority on 7th, so I had no reference as to what to expect. I had read their veggie burgers were very good. At any rate, food was good, especially their desserts. I don't know if their pricing is sort of a spin on the joint's punk attitude. Hm, if so, I'd rather go there and have coffee (excellent) and drink their seltzer (very special, generated by an imported Japanese machine), whilst aligning with punk stance and saying, "Food is death! Do not eat!"

Inferiority Burger is the apt name for this place. Tasteless food that is thankfully minimal in quantity. Inapt service  - a hostess who's exaspareted by the fact that our group of three is planning to order from the main menu at 4.50 pm while knowing that the place doesn't begin to serve the full menu before 5 pm. "This is very confusing for us", she says and sighs dramatically. So did we after leaving $190 for a couple of miniscule but equally inedible dishes. As a bonus the restaurant did NOT offer toilet paper. Way to go GREEN.
https://www.nytimes.com/2024/03/14/style/superiority-burger-ashwin-deshmukh.html?smid=nytcore-ios-share&referringSource=articleShare&sgrp=c-cb

The Asian hostess tonight told me that the wait is an hour long. So I went outside to meet my friends and out of curiosity, one of them came in to ask for a table and was given one right away! How does that make sense? Ageist? Racist? Who knows?! 

The food is NOT good. Better off eating vegan burger at Bare Burger to be honest. And yes, that Asian hostess is a horrible human.

We were able to snag a couple seats in the back by the bar. I had a beer and we shared the superiority burger currently priced at $18. I'm it's a vegetarian burger; I'm not sure what the patty consisted of.

One of the most over-priced, mid tier burgers I've ever had in my life. Truly awful. What a terrible establishment. The only thing saving the meal was how much we were laughing at how over priced the food was.
I never comment on service but they made us feel unwelcome and rushed us even though it was an a off hour on a Monday with few customers. Food was good but nothing extraordinary

A great experience!! Super lively, lot of chatter, retro diner feel, and great service!

This all vegetarian restaurant sketched me out at first, but the food was super flavorful and made with love! The burger was great, the collard green sandwich was good too. It's a place you def have to try! The prices however... kinda expensive for the portion sizes. The food was great but prefer real meat any day. Still, def worth the try
Delicious food and a chill ambiance, perfect vibe summarizing this neighborhood. Loved the lunch menu options, looking forward to going back for dinner and drinks

Your favorite restaurant's favorite restaurant! 

Dishes arrive on the smaller side so order 1-2 extra items. Arrive before doors open on a weekday to snag a spot during the first seating to avoid an hour's wait. Alternative: show up for their late night after hours menu and try to snag a fresh made Chrissy's Pizza! 

Will def need to come back for the dessert case.
It makes me sad when places do the arnold palmer with lemon juice not lemonade . Adn unsweet tea. Didnt get to try the food yet

i do not understand the hype. eating here felt like a fever dream. like sitting in an overpriced vegan diner in an alternate universe but the food is made by a friend who is a great home cook but oversalts their food. i'm sure the pricing has to do with equitable business practices or something (i hope so at least) but even the service was weird hahaha anyways i think there's a lot tastier and creative vegan restaurants in nyc probably. the date shake was really yummy at least but sooo tiny

Wow... I'm surprised at how underwhelmed my food and experience was. Having been a lactose intolerant vegetarian the past 14 years, any vegetarian restaurant gets my attention. This place always has a line outside, so after stumbling by with no line, I decided to pop in for dinner before meeting friends later.

I was promptly seated at the bar at 7:02 and handed a water and a menu. I already intended to order the namesake burger, but took a quick gander. After the waitress circled back, I placed my order, no drink, no bells or whistles. Settling into my book, I was shocked when my order quickly arrived at 7:07. It was small for a US-sized burger, and for being priced at $18. Considering the going rate in NYC is about $19 for a burger and fries, this seemed steep.

Taking a bite, I quickly was met with disappointment. Sure, the bun was pillowy like a potato bun, but it was small and quickly smooshed and devoured, much like a McDonalds burger. Considering I was seated, ordered, ate, paid my bill, and left the sit-down restaurant by 7:17, this hardly felt any different than McDonalds other than feeling a bit ripped off. The patty itself was no more exciting than a mushy black bean burger (which, by the way, is not exciting at all).

Their sides are $10 and up, served on the same size plate as their small burgers but listed as "shareable". I'm less than 100 pounds and nothing looked shareable about their portions to me. Considering the many vegan options here in NY, I would say spend your money elsewhere. If you never eat vegan/vegetarian food, maybe this will intrigue you, otherwise I think you'll be underwhelmed.

This is ridiculous, sure the burger is "good" but nothing incredible or worth going back for when it's 18 DOLLARS and comes with no sides and will be scarfed down in three bites. This place is a total rip-off.

***They do not serve fries, tots or anything of the sort. Yes, the sign above the restaurant that says "burgers & fries"is lying*** Met up with some family at this -ok- vegetarian/accidentally vegan spot for an early bird 5pm dinner. There was a decent line at 5pm and they don't take rezies, so queue up home slice! 

The food is...mid and expensive. Service was A+, really good, very  attentive. The space is a nice mix of retro, deco and fun. Bathroom is super clean! The music is a great mix of things most people won't know but you'll feel cool when you do. Blame inflation or nyc rent but the meal felt pricey for what it was. Had the burger, tried the collard green sandwich, white sweet potato, sweet n sour beats and the cornbread with lentils. It was all, ok. The focaccia, burger buns and corn bread are the standouts. The potato was (in fairness) better than ok. The burger paddy was smallish with a mustardy overtone but not bad. The rest was kind out forgettable. We also tried the house soda. Very small for $10, just ok. I personally didn't find the taste /quantity worth the price. Dessert outshines the mains here tbh. The gelato flavors change frequently. We had chocolate/mint - deep mint flavor. Like, mint from leaf not a lab. It was delicious! Also had a "scoop" of a lemony flavored gelato which was also delish! The scoops are actually  spoonfuls, you get two scoops served in an icy cup. We also had the pearl pie which all agreed was the best they had to offer. So good!

The burger is just ok. However, the focaccia sandwich and the desserts exceeded all my expectations. Inside, I love the classic nyc diner vibe with a retro modern touch. The place is always busy and the servers are so nice. I would come back for the pies any day.

A pricy, but excellent, mostly vegetarian/vegan counter-service restaurant serving excellent sandwiches and burgers, and a great focaccia. I found the pies to be ordinary, but my meal was a blessing. Service is attentive, if a little slow, especially in a lunch rush, but I'd go back.
I think the main things this place has going for it is service and ambiance. It has a cool retro vibe and great attentive servers. I thought the burger was alright, nothing standout

My wife and I flew into JFK at like 10PM -- had to wait for a checked bag, then grab a taxi to Manhattan. Took forever. By the time we checked into our room at the Standard in East Village and got settled, we were STARVING.

One problem: It was a Thursday night and most restaurants were already closed or closing. And since we were looking for vegan, the problem was compounded.

We asked our daughter for advice and she suggested Superiority. Thank God she did.

Superiority was GREAT, and open until 2AM. 

Late-night menu was limited, but we were very happy with the choices. I got a Trumer Pils beer, my wife the "best seltzer water in NYC," and we ordered a bunch of food: the TFT sandwich, pasta e fagioli soup, some sort of cauliflower thing -- all super tasty -- especially the TFT and the soup. Really good.

Superiority -- you saved our lives. For that I thank you.

ordered the tomato soup and the superiority burger. tomato soup was good but a bit bland -- personally would not order again. however, the burger was delicious! one of the better vegetarian burgers, without just a black bean patty. would recommend ordered extra tomato's on the side (they are roasted, and def add to the flavor) overall, would recommend

An unpretentious vegan restaurant--playful and super fun, with an uncomplicated menu. I think you either get this place or you don't, and judging from the frequent lines, plenty of people get it, and those who don't are apt to judge it too harshly. I'm a big fan of old school veggie burgers done well, so I absolutely love this place. Yes the burger is mushy, and yes that's just how I like it! I've tasted a few other things, and they were all good, but it's the namesake burger that will bring me back. A bit pricey? Perhaps. But so is everything else these days. Service is attentive, charming, and speedy, which is great because you can eat and get on with your life.

I've been wanting to try this spot for forever so I'm glad my friend and I were able to casually get a table at around 9:00PM on a Thursday. We both ordered the soda special (guava orange mango) and it was very refreshing. 

My friend is a vegetarian so he really appreciated that this place is all vegetarian/vegan. We both tried the superiority burger and enjoyed it. However it is a MESS. The patty doesn't hold up very well so everything falls apart. I don't like tomatoes or pickles and they were happy to substitute them for the fried onions in mine- great addition. 

The highlight of the meal was the pea shoots with spicy mushrooms. Amazing flavors (not too spicy, not too saucy-oily) and great texture of the pea shoots. 

I was really looking forward to the gelato bc so many people rave about it. It was really great but I'm slightly annoyed that they force you into getting 2 scoops. Both flavors (peach and I believe butterscotch pecan?) I got ended up being so good I didn't mind in the end but I think it's a strange rule. 

Overall, I wasn't totally blown away but I would come back to get the pea shoots and I'd be interested in trying their other veggie sides/collard greens sandwich.

Highlights: date milkshake, beets, and sour cherry ice cream sandwich

Skip: Superiority burger (not bad just not great) 

Awesome chill atmosphere. Stick to the shake sides and dessert and its a great great meal!

I came here in a group of 4 without a reservation at approximately 9 PM on a Thursday night and waited ~5 min for a table.

Food / Drink:  They have COFFEE thank goodness. It definitely fits the atmosphere they have (looks like a diner). We had some spectacular food including a few yuba dishes and some spicy greens. A big plus is that all food options are VEGETARIAN and a majority are vegan (or at least vegan accommodating). I had perhaps the best dessert I have ever had in my entire life (pearl pie) that was the ideal mix of a muted sweet custard with a wonderful crust. Consistent with prior recommendations, we passed on the burger itself.

Atmosphere:  Diner vibes and also open late night apparently. We enjoyed our time so much that we went back again the next TWO nights in order to try their "late-night" menu (including the much-hyped tofu fried chicken sandwich) but for an unknown reason, they were not open!? Nothing on social media or online - so this was unfortunately quite disappointing.

Service:  Unfortunately quite average to even a bit below average if I'm being honest. It feels a bit like they know how good their food is...?

I wish I could rave and "strongly recommend" this place and my rating feels high? I would prefer to give a 3.5 due to the lack of reliable hours (without any posts online!) Thankfully, I was quite nearby and it wasn't a big deal, but I would have been so disappointed if I traveled across the city late at night for this...

I went to this place for the first time two days ago by myself and had the wedge salad and Superiority burger. I had read all the reviews and was expecting to find the portions small, food overpriced, staff snotty, etc. Instead, I was blown away. The food was perfection, the portions plentiful (this is quality food, people!), the staff quietly perfect (smart and attentive). I was a solo diner and they didn't mind my request to sit at a table instead of the counter, and I saw the owner-chef hard at work even first thing in the morning (that is, "morning" in East Village time). Whoever made that wedge salad today knew what they were doing and had the courage of their convictions (lots of pepper, lots of acid, very fresh). I'm not rich,  but I'll be back. It was 100% worth it. total bill $37.00 plus $12.00 tip = $50.00 for a real treat. Well done Brooks and crew.

Had a really lovely dining experience, my server, as well as the manager was very kind and attentive. The burger I had was delicious. As was the pearl pie. One of the best desserts ive had possibly ever. Was grateful it was recommended to me. Happy to have visited such a cute & vegan friendly diner.

I don't understand why Superiority Burger doesn't have a higher rating. I went there on a sweltering Monday and ordered the tofu-fried tofu sandwich and a beet salad. The salad was the perfect antidote to the slumpy weather with its crisp, sweet-and-sour beets, fresh dill, piquant dressing, and, best of all, little fried pretzel pieces that took that salad and elevated it to the level of a treat. So many flavors and textures, from salty to sweet to sour to crisp to creamy to firm and crunchy, with the jewel tones of the beets complemented by the green, feathery dill, white dressing, and earthy pretzel nuggets. So far so good!

Then, the tofu sandwich. If you're a vegetarian like me, you've tried your share of bean curd and you know that a slab of tofu as the centerpiece of a dish carries a red light warning of potential sogginess and blandness. This tofu had a smoked flavor and texture that struck the right balance between watery and meaty, with a perfectly crisp breading. Toothsome indeed, but enhanced by slaw, dressing, and what must have been a homemade sesame-studded focaccia. So far, lunch was outstanding.  

Dessert was the only less-than-perfect dish; I ordered a vegan tutti-frutti cake made of polenta and coconut with a colorful fruit topping. It was too sweet, with a strange, candy-like flavor. Eh, it was still dessert, and who can blame the kitchen for experimenting? 

The server was kind to me in my disheveled, sweat-logged state and poured me many cups of water as I raved about the food.

As a postscript, I've been hankering to try this place ever since it opened, and have been thwarted various times.
